#UNIT Unit 1 | Photosynthesis | 12 | en
Photosynthesis is how green plants make food. Inside chloro-
plasts, chlorophyll captures sunlight. The plant combines carbon dioxide
from the air with water from the soil to make glucose, and releases oxygen.
12
Plants store extra glucose as starch in roots, seeds and leaves.
#UNIT Unit 2 | The cell | 28 | en
The cell is the basic unit of life. The nucleus holds the genetic material and controls the cell.
The cell membrane decides what enters and leaves. Mitochondria release energy from food.
28
#UNIT Unit 3 | Water cycle | 41 | en
In the water cycle, the sun heats water and it evaporates into vapour. Rising vapour cools and
condenses into clouds. Water then falls as precipitation such as rain, and flows back to rivers and the sea.
#UNIT Unit 4 | Force and motion | 57 | en
A force can change how an object moves. Newton's second law says force equals mass times
acceleration. The same force gives a lighter object a larger acceleration than a heavier one.
#UNIT Unit 5 | Density | 70 | en
Density is mass divided by volume. An object floats in water if its density is lower than the
density of water, about 1 gram per cubic centimetre, and sinks if its density is higher.
#UNIT Unit 6 | Acids and bases | 84 | en
The pH scale runs from 0 to 14. Acids have a pH below 7 and turn blue litmus paper red.
Bases have a pH above 7 and turn red litmus paper blue. Pure water is neutral at pH 7.
#UNIT Unit 7 | Electric circuits | 99 | en
An electric circuit is a closed path for current. In a series circuit there is one path, so if one
bulb fails all the others go out. In a parallel circuit each bulb has its own path, so the others keep working.
#UNIT Unit 8 | Soil | 112 | en
Soil is made of weathered rock, air, water and decayed plant and animal matter called humus.
Fertile soil holds water and nutrients that crops such as teff and maize need to grow.
